findings.text: the run-to-project scan now calls runs._promoted_record_project, which resolves the registry again through runs._mounted_project_roots -> flight.mounted_project_docs, so a derivation costs one parse per ref instead of one per pass; instrumenting flight.mounted_project_docs and calling wait_projects_for over three run refs measured 4 reads, and 7 when the registry is unreadable, against the docstring promise at :1853 of one read for the whole list and the commit's claim of one read per derivation. This regresses the exact economy the node was previously reviewed on and makes every admission pass grow with the number of unresolved run refs.

the assertion counts queue_admission._mounted_projects while the delta routes the scan through flight.mounted_project_docs, so it holds at 1 whatever the real read count is; widening it to the flight seam is what would have caught the regression above, and the durability score is docked because this guard is blind to it.

the fragment states a pass costs one registry parse rather than one per unresolved ref, and that the eighth case shows a run wait parses the registry once; measured through the seam the code actually uses, three refs cost four parses, so the landed evidence asserts a figure the code contradicts.

when a caller passes mounted=None, meaning the registry could not be read, wait_project_lookup calls _mounted_projects_and_failure again for every ref, so the unreadable path pays a second read per ref (7 attempts for three refs, measured) and can resolve different refs of one pass against different read outcomes if the registry recovers mid-pass, which the docstring at :1855 says does not happen.
